title: Long ages of abundant life preceded the lowest Silurian strata

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Long ages of abundant life preceded the lowest Silurian strata

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: If descent with modification is true, periods at least as long as the whole time from the Silurian to the present must have passed before the lowest Silurian strata were laid down, and during them the world swarmed with living creatures.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. IX: On the Imperfection of the Geological Record

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Consequently, if my theory be true, it is indisputable that before the lowest Silurian stratum was deposited, long periods elapsed, as long as, or probably far longer than, the whole interval from the Silurian age to the present day; and that during these vast, yet quite unknown, periods of time, the world swarmed with living creatures.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter IX, “On the Imperfection of the Geological Record”; section “On their sudden appearance in the lowest known fossiliferous strata”. Scope: life on earth before the oldest then-known (Cambro-Silurian) fossiliferous strata

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch09-13: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.72

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Public fossil and geochronological records strongly test the existence and duration of pre-Silurian life. They only partially resolve global abundance and Darwin's specific claim that the earlier interval was at least as long.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Estimate the age and diversity of pre-Silurian life from radiometrically dated fossils, biomarkers, and molecular-clock analyses. Compare the duration before the Silurian and evidence of abundance with the Silurian-to-present interval and a minimal-life alternative.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Early molecular clocks have broad calibration uncertainty.

Soft-bodied Precambrian life has a highly incomplete record.

'Swarmed' lacks a precise abundance threshold.

fields.value:

operationalizability: 0.7
analysis feasibility: 0.7
data existence: 0.86
data adequacy: 0.62

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The duration comparison is a direct arithmetic use of the geologic time scale, and Precambrian fossils are public even though they are sparse. The mapping from Darwin's Silurian onto the Cambrian is historically standard. Abundance of life is less sharp than the time comparison, but the existence of a long earlier biosphere is decidable with current compilations.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare the radiometric duration before Darwin's lowest fossiliferous strata, mapped to the base of the Cambrian, with the duration from that horizon to the present, and score whether fossils or biomarkers show widespread life through the earlier interval. A shorter pre-Cambrian span, or a span lacking evidence of life, would refute the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Lowest Silurian in the 1859 text has to be aligned with the modern base of the Cambrian.

Swarmed is qualitative, and the early record is mostly microbial and concentrated in particular facies.
